assessment_summary.cou_name: Set safe power/irrigation envelopes for a 7F open-irrigated RF ablation catheter in the left atrium; decision metric: peak 3 mm tissue temperature and lesion depth/width after 30–60 s

evidence_keywords: Unit tests for UDF I/O and mapping pass CI on each commit
run scripts in a Singularity container
UDF Git tag rfcht-v1.7 (commit 9f4a1b2)
tracked by DVC with SHA links to raw data
External SME (Dr. R. Ghuman) performed a red-team read
custom heat-source UDF and perfusion toggle
artificially forced benchmark
closed-form temperature field
Energy residual over the control volume was <0.2% at steady state
Four meshes (1.2M to 9.6M cells)
observed order 1.96 for peak temperature
extrapolated discretization effect 3.8% on peak temp
Time-step halving from 5 ms to 2.5 ms shifts peak temperature by 0.6 C
Second-order discretization, coupled solver
Residuals <1e-6
monitored integral energy plateaus within 0.3% over last 10 s
Input decks, meshes, and outputs tracked by DVC
run scripts in a Singularity container
Lab team provided blinded validation files
re-ran one case from scratch on a different workstation
3D conjugate thermal-fluid model of blood, saline jets, electrode, epoxy, and myocardium
laminar assumed but bracketed with SST k-omega for sensitivity
Tissue perfusion via Pennes term
We explicitly do not claim fidelity for steam pops, charring
Inputs and ranges
Tissue thermal/electrical properties (±15% about literature)
contact pressure (10–20 kPa)
Posterior mean contact conductance 7.5 kW/m^2-K
12 benchtop perfused-myocardium tests (porcine)
fiber-optic probes at 3 and 5 mm
Lesion dimensions from 7T MRI (0.2 mm voxel)
25–45 W and 17–30 mL/min
two blood speeds (0.15, 0.25 m/s)
esophageal wall as an isothermal boundary 37.0±0.2 C
Catheter contact angle 15°
applied RF power 25–50 W with PI control matching generator logs
contact pressure 10–20 kPa producing 0.2–0.5 mm indentation
esophageal wall as an isothermal boundary 37.0±0.2 C at 4 mm posterior
Mean absolute temperature error at 3 mm = 2.1 C
Normalized RMS error on lesion depth = 9%; width = 11%
all cases fall within a 95% total-error band
One outlier at 45 W/0.15 m/s under-predicts depth by 15%
